Gane (14-2, 1 NC) stands at No. 18 in the MMA Fighting Pound-for-Pound Rankings and was recently promoted to undisputed heavyweight champion in the absence of incumbent Tom Aspinall. The circumstances are certainly controversial, with Gane being responsible for Aspinall’s current stint on the injury list due to eye pokes suffered in a title defense against Gane in October 2025. Gane soldiered on, defeating former two-division UFC champion Alex Pereira via knockout at UFC White House to claim an interim belt, which put him in position to become the division’s sole titleholder with Aspinall still on the mend.

The clear-cut choice for 2026 Breakthrough Fighter of the Year, Hokit (10-0) can cap off an unbelievable run to the top of the heavyweight division by upsetting the more experienced Gane. Hokit has drawn plenty of headlines for his bizarre and offensive comments, but when fight night rolls around, he has impressed. The onetime NFL hopeful ran through his first two UFC opponents before coming out on top of an insane Fight of the Year candidate brawl against Curtis Blaydes, and then made the most of his UFC White House opportunity by demolishing fan favorite Derrick Lewis. Now, Hokit has the chance to become UFC champion just 15 months after earning his contract on Dana White’s Contender Series.

This is the UFC 334 live blog for Kayla Harrison vs. Amanda Nunes, bantamweight championship co-main event Saturday at Madison Square Garden in New York.

Harrison (19-1) is currently No. 3 in the MMA Fighting Pound-for-Pound Rankings. A two-time Olympic gold medalist in judo (the only American to achieve that feat), Harrison took the MMA world by storm, winning her first 15 pro fights and a pair of PFL lightweight tournaments. She won the UFC bantamweight championship with a submission over Julianna Pena, setting the stage for a long-awaited showdown with Nunes, who retired in 2023.

Nunes (23-5) previously trained with Harrison at American Top Team, but Harrison’s rise through the ranks always raised the question whether they could ever meet in the cage. While Harrison was just starting off, Nunes was in the middle of one of the most dominant runs in MMA history, going on a 14-1 run from 2015-2023 that included claiming titles at bantamweight and featherweight and successfully defending those belts a total of eight times. Now, “The Lioness” steps back into the octagon with a chance to add to her already all-time great legacy.

Check out the UFC 334 live blog for Kayla Harrison vs. Amanda Nunes below.

Preamble

It took years to get here, but it’s finally happening: Kayla Harrison. Amanda Nunes. Let’s go!

Always tell me the odds

Just about a coin toss per FanDuel, with Harrison the favorite at -158 and Nunes a slight underdog at +134. Man, seeing Nunes as an underdog… feels strange, man.

Round 1

Blake Grice oversees the bantamweight championship co-main event.

Feinting and footwork in the middle of the octagon, neither fighter giving an inch. Neither fighter throwing much out there either. Nunes lets her hands go as Harrison keeps her distance, there’s a right hand that has Harrison retreating. Good leg kick by Nunes. Harrison changes levels but eats a counter right. There’s another hard right by Nunes. The champ is feeling these. Harrison desperate to clinch, it looks like Nunes hit her with something in close. One-way traffic for The Lioness right now.

Harrison with a much-needed body lock, but Nunes not letting her get comfortable and she slips out of there. Nunes on the prowl, looking to strike. Harrison ducks a punch and lands a well-timed takedown, Nunes back up, but Harrison stays connected and lands a trademark judo throw. She has one of Nunes’ arms trapped and she’s landing a lot of unanswered punches, nothing too damaging, though. Nunes throwing her legs up, trying to shift the balance, but Harrison just staying heavy and keeping Nunes’ arm in a bad position.

Will the judges favor Nunes’ heavy punches on the feet or Harrison’s sustained ground offense?

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Nunes.

Round 2

Nunes surprisingly willing to engage with Harrison and she’s actually going for takedowns as they wrestle along the fence. Curious.

Harrison angling for a trip. Nunes keeping her hips and legs out of danger for now. Not much to score in this round, but Nunes isn’t giving up on the grappling. She actually manages to drag Harrison down, that was impressive. Harrison back up to the feet with Nunes hanging on to a body lock. But it’s Harrison who is setting her up as she hits the same throw she did in Round 1 and now with a lot more time to work and a lot less damage done up to this point.

Nunes is stuck and even though Harrison isn’t landing fight-ending shots, she’s pretty much shut Nunes out this round. If Round 1 was close, this is a clear Harrison round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Harrison. Overall, 19-19.

Round 3

Nunes coming forward with straight punches, wisely keeping her distance for now. Harrison lunges forward to grapple, Nunes changes levels and teases a takedown before backing away again. Harrison catches a kick and goes in for a takedown, reversal by Nunes and she’s on top against the cage, but this might be exactly where Harrison wants her.

Nunes actually advances to mount, Harrison gets away with a cage grab to avoid getting into a worse position. She scrambles out and manages to bring the fight back to the feet. Harrison wants to set up a throw, Nunes blocks it and scores a trip. Nunes briefly takes Harrison’s back, Harrison working to spin into Nunes’ guard. She gets there.

Elbow from top position by Harrison. And another one that cuts Nunes open, followed by a good punch. Nunes creates some separation, but is lacking the explosion to get up and she eats another big elbow. Big finish to the round for Harrison.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Harrison. Overall, 29-28 Harrison.

Round 4

Nunes tentatively coming forward and throwing strikes, Harrison eventually shuts it down with an aggressive clinch. Nunes separates and connects with a hard left. Harrison snatches a leg and trips Nunes, sending her scrambling away. Harrison seizes the opportunity, easily taking Nunes’ back and securing a rear-naked choke. Nunes taps! AND STILL!

Official result: Kayla Harrison def. Amanda Nunes via submission (rear-naked choke) (R4, 1:29)

Post-fight

Harrison is in shock at everything that just happened.

“It feels surreal. Sometimes I can’t believe my life. I was sexually abused at a young age and statistically I’m not supposed to be here. So to go from that, if you told me at six years old, if you had told me at 16 years old this would be my life, I wouldn’t believe you, and I’m just really grateful. I’m humbled and it’s an honor and a privilege to stand before you.”

As for what’s next, Harrison says she has a lot of decisions to make and “we’ll see.” She needs time to rest and recover from injuries.

No interview for Nunes, unfortunately.

It wasn’t always pretty but Caio Borralho used his grappling to maintain control and get the win over Yousri Belgaroui at UFC 334.

Repeated takedowns followed by ground control allowed Borralho to wear down the kickboxer over three rounds as Belgaroui just couldn’t get much offense going. When it was over the judges all scored the fight 30-27 as the Brazilian got the victory.

“I’m happy,” Borralho said after the win. “I came to this fight there are levels in the game. I came in here to show that my experience, this is my 10th fight in the UFC. I came to this fight to show that. There are levels to this game my guys. It’s the belt hunt season. Get ready motherf*ckers. I always call out Dricus .. I’m not going to waste my time so one thing I want is my rematch with [Nassourdine] Imavov. I’m ready, I’m connected. It could be Brandon [Allen\ but I want Imavov.”

Borralho actually connected with a good left hand to start the fight and Belgaroui fired back with an effective body kick. Borralho then followed with a takedown attempt but Belgaroui defended, although the Brazilian was relentless to draw the fight to the ground.

Borralho then jumped on the back as he locked on the body triangle and started searching for submissions. Borralho nearly locked on a face crank as Belgaroui was stuck playing defense on the ground against an expert grappler.

Belgaroui scrambled to break free with Borralho stuck looking for a guillotine choke while holding onto head control before fighters got back to the feet again.

On the restart in round two, Belgaroui looked much more comfortable throwing his kicks and not allowing Borralho to establish his grappling. But a knee up the middle gave Borralho the chance to close the distance but he couldn’t maintain control enough for a takedown.

Borralho was patient until he got the body lock but he still couldn’t put Belgaroui on the ground. Belgaroui then connected withi a good knee to the body but Borralho fired right back with his hands.

Borralho then found the opening to finally get Belgaroui back to the mat again as he moved into side control. The Brazilian landed another takedown in the final round as he maintained control over Belgaroui.

This is the UFC 334 live blog for Caio Borralho vs. Yousri Belgaroui, the main card middleweight bout Saturday at Madison Square Garden in New York.

Borralho (18-2, 1 NC) is currently No. 5 at 185 pounds in the MMA Fighting Global Rankings. Despite having won eight of his nine UFC appearances, Borralho finds himself having to defend his spot rather than angle for a title shot. It doesn’t help that he’s fought several of the other contenders in his division already. Following a loss to Nassourdine Imavov in September, Borralho rebounded with a unanimous decision win over Reinier de Ridder at UFC 326.

A former adversary and now training partner of former two-division UFC champion Alex Pereira, Belgaroui (11-3) has quickly established himself as one of the most dangerous standup threats in the middleweight division. The Dutch kickboxer has defeated his first three UFC opponents, all by knockout, most recently needing less than a round to put away Djorden Santos.

Check out the UFC 334 live blog for Caio Borralho vs. Yousri Belgaroui below.

Preamble and Odds

Caio Borralho with a risky fight here, he goes in as the -156 underdog per FanDuel. Belgaroui an intriguing underdog at +132.

Round 1

Keith Peterson the referee for this featured middleweight bout.

Belgaroui towers over Borralho (as he does over most of his opponents). Borralho scores first with a left hand. He’s beating Belgaroui to the punch, then goes for a takedown. Let’s see how Belgaroui’s takedown defense holds up. Belgaroui fighting to drag Belgaroui down, he ends up on Belgaroui’s back. Borralho secures a body triangle with a lot of time to work.

Belgaroui struggling as Borralho gets heavy, now they’re on the mat with Borralho stuck to Belgaroui’s back. Borralho fighting the hands, he wants that choke. Belgaroui scrambling and nearly ends up with Borralho in mount, but he’s creating space. Borralho attacks with a guillotine, Belgaroui staying calm and he’s in a safer position even with Borralho hanging on to him.

Belgaroui lost the round, but his grappling defense held up enough to make it to the next round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Borralho.

Round 2

Belgaroui confidently marching forward and throwing long strikes, we’ll see how Borralho deals with this pressure. Belgaroui sniping away as Borralho looks for an opening to grapple. Borralho takes a knee as he changes levels, but he has Belgaroui backed up against the fence. And they separate!

Borralho scores with a right hand, then shoots in. A little under three minutes to work, Belgaroui showing good balance. Borralho gets to the back again, though, and he has the advantage. Belgaroui fighting the hands well and he’s able to turn in to Borralho. Borralho lands a couple of good punches. Borralho in for another takedown, absorbing a knee to the body for his troubles.

Borralho with a takedown and he’ll end the round in side control.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Belgaroui. Overall, 19-19.

Round 3

Belgaroui with a snapping leg kick. Front kick to the body. Borralho taking his time, he might be confident he’s up on the scorecards. Nice jab by Borralho. Double leg by Borralho and that’s the easiest takedown he’s scored the whole fight. Borralho fighting to secure the legs, Belgaroui gripping a wrist. Belgaroui back up to the feet and briefly threatens with a guillotine, but Borralho shrugs it off. They’re back at striking range with half a round to go.

Belgaroui having success with knees to the body, not sure how much that will resonate with judges with no follow-up. High knee connects for Belgaroui, that’s going to make an impression for sure. Borralho tags him with a right hand. Definitive shots few and far between, neither gas tank looking particularly fool. Borralho telegraphs a takedown and gets it on an exhausted Belgaroui. Less than a minute to go and this could be where the fighters stay for the remainder of the contest.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Borralho. Overall, 29-28 Borralho.

Official result: Caio Borralho def. Yousri Belgaroui via unanimous decision (30-27 x3)

Post-fight

Borralho says he wanted to show there were “levels to this game,” and he wasn’t focused on making a statement by finishing Belgaroui. He says he didn’t feel like Belgaroui was a step above him in the standup.

“I’m ready for the belt. Just like Jean Silva and Carlos Prates. It’s the belt-hunt season, get ready for it motherf*ckers. The Fighting Nerds are taking over.”

If not a title fight, Borralho says he’s not wasting his time with another Dricus du Plessis callout. If Sean Strickland isn’t going to defend the middleweight title against Nassourine Imavov, Borralho suggests a rematch with Imavov for an interim title.

This is the UFC 334 live blog for Uros Medic vs. Kevin Holland, the main card welterweight bout Saturday at Madison Square Garden in New York.

Medic (14-3) is on an incredible hot streak with first-round knockout victories in his past four appearances, a run that currently has him at No. 12 at 170 pounds in the MMA Fighting Global Rankings. The Serbian standout picked up the biggest win of his career this past August when he headlined in his home country at UFC Belgrade and delivered with a 30-second TKO over veteran contender Daniel Rodriguez. Win or lose, “The Doctor” has never gone to the scorecards.

The always active Holland (29-15, 1 NC) recently got back in the win column with a unanimous decision win over Randy Brown at UFC 327 this past April. Holland has been somewhat sedated this fight week, but he almost always brings it in the octagon, with 11 UFC finishes to his name.

Check out the UFC 334 live blog for Uros Medic vs. Kevin Holland below.

Preamble

Can Uros Medic pick up another first-round knockout and cement his case for a top 10 opponent? It’s always risky to overlook Kevin Holland.

Always tell me the odds

Medic a slight favorite at -164, a good amount of respect being shown to the always dangerous Holland at +138 (per FanDuel).

Round 1

Marc Goddard the referee for this welterweight matchup.

Both fighters with range-finding strikes to start. Medic slips on a kick that catches Holland’s shoulder, which draws a chuckle from Holland. He’s letting the trash talk go already. Loud right hand by Medic, but Holland just ate it and landed a counter. Body kick by Medic. Another wild kick by Medic and he sends himself flying to the mat. Wacky stuff. Holland with a series of uppercuts and he pushes Medic over, don’t think that was a knockdown. They’re back up, Holland with a slick trip. Where did that come from? Holland attacking with a ninja choke. It looks tight, but Medic has juuuuuuust enough room to breathe. Medic fights out of it, Holland right back on it. Medic fights out of it again! That was tense.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Holland.

Round 2

Commentary points out Medic could be having an issue with his left knee. Big kick to the groin by Medic, we need to pause the action here. Ow.

Back at it. They clash and it’s Medic who gets the better of it with a straight left. Holland working to control distance with long kicks to the body and leg. Medic lands a left hand again, he’s getting close. There’s a right hand from Holland. Medic with a left. Big strikes few and far between in this round, they’re showing a lot of respect for each other’s power. And then there’s another low blow by Medic.

Long delay here. Not sure if Goddard will take a point or not. Probably should?

And there it is! One-point deduction for Medic and we’re back on with a little under two minutes to go in the round.

Holland goes for a takedown, they scramble on the ground, Medic with the advantage and he lands a few good punches as Holland secures a body lock and stands up, pushing Medic to the fence.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-8, Holland. Overall, 20-17 Holland.

Round 3

Left hand catches Holland coming in, he’s quick to grapple. He’s using his size to push Medic to the fence. Medic working to circle out, but Holland keeps him locked up. Clinch battle along the fence, this isn’t good for Medic. Surprisingly, Goddard steps in for a reset. Don’t know about that call.

Clubbing left for Medic, that was a moment there, but he can’t follow up. Glancing shot from Medic gets a reaction from Holland, but Medic backs off, maybe he thought Holland was complaining about a foul? Unclear. Medic with a little over a minute to find a finish and salvage this one. Medic scores with a left. Last 30 seconds, Medic lands and Holland is rocked. Another left connects, Holland hurt, but Medic is running out of time. He’s not going to get it.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Medic. Overall, 29-27 Holland.

Official result: Uros Medic vs. Kevin Holland ends in a majority draw (29-28, 28-28 x2)

Apologies for the delay on the result there, but Bruce Buffer read the scores as, and I quote, “30-27, 29-28, 28-28” and said it was a majority draw, which confused everyone from the fighters to the commentators crowd to the poor bastards out there who have to live blog these things. But I think draw is correct.

Just an absolute mess of a fight from beginning to end.

Luis Gurule defied the odds with a huge upset win to hand Bilal Hasan the first loss of his professional career at UFC 334. While the night started out rough for Gurule, he bounced back in the second and third rounds by taking Hasan to the ground and controlling him with his wrestling. When it […]

Luis Gurule defied the odds with a huge upset win to hand Bilal Hasan the first loss of his professional career at UFC 334.

While the night started out rough for Gurule, he bounced back in the second and third rounds by taking Hasan to the ground and controlling him with his wrestling. When it was over, the judges scored the contest 29-28 and 29-28 for Gurule with the third official going 29-28 for Hasan after three hard rounds.

That was still enough for Gurule to get the job done as he pulls off one of the biggest wins of his career.

“Chat GPT don’t know shit,” Gurule shouted after his victory. “F*ck the odds. F*ck the haters. I’m so happy. Look there’s only 10 people that believed in me, and it feels f*cking good. I dragged him into deep waters. I knew he couldn’t swim.”

Hasan opened with some quick kicks including one to the head that definitely got Gurule’s attention. Hasan kept chipping away to the legs and then going back up to the head as Gurule struggled to close the distance.

Hasan also opened up with his punches as well but Gurule was quick to fire back and he landed a solid counter right hand that scored a flash knockdown. Hasan bounced back but that shot definitely got his attention.

The striking attacks from Hasan continued into the second round as he varied up his offense with kicks and punches. Hasan eventually uncorked a spinning back fist but Gurule blocked it effectively before a perfectly timed takedown.

With Gurule on top, he pressed Hasan towards the cage while working to unleash his ground and pound. Gurule stayed busy with punches and elbows until time expired in the round.

Gurule opened the final round with another takedown but he also ended up with a cut over his eye that was pouring blood from an inside elbow. Gurule kept peppering away from the top position to maintain control and prevent a potential standup.

Hasan tried throwing up submissions from the bottom but Gurule wouldn’t allow him to break free as time ran out in the fight.

A close fight throughout but Gurule’s top control and dominant ground work obviously got the job done as he scores a huge win while Hasan has to go back to the drawing board after suffering the first loss of his career.

This is the UFC 334 live blog for Bilal Hasan vs. Luis Gurule, the main card flyweight bout Saturday at Madison Square Garden in New York.

Just 25 years old, Hasan (10-0, 1 NC) is one of the brightest prospects on the UFC’s 125-pound roster. Hasan earned a contract on Dana White’s Contender Series this past August with a 45-second knockout over Mridul Saikia and then made a quick turnaround just 18 days later for his octagon debut at UFC Shanghai. He didn’t disappoint, putting away fellow undefeated prospect Nilson Rojas with a highlight-reel knockout punch in the second round.

Gurule (11-4) is a massive underdog looking to spoil Hasan’s numbered event debut. “Grim” holds a decision win over Daniel Barez in the UFC, but has otherwise struggled to find success with the promotion, going just 1-4 since debuting in April 2025. His most recent outing ended inside of a round as he was submitted by Rei Tsuruya.

Check out the UFC 334 live blog for Bilal Hasan vs. Luis Gurule below.

Preamble

All aboard the hype train for Bilal Hasan! In just his second UFC appearance, Hasan gets a main card spot at Madison Square Garden. Is it too much too soon?

Always tell me the odds

According to FanDuel, Hasan is an absurd -1150 favorite. In his second UFC fight! Don’t bet on MMA. Gurule a massive underdog at +730.

Round 1

Kevin MacDonald referees the main card opener.

Hasan opens up with kicks to the leg and body, he’s off to a fast start. Spin kick to the body connects for Hasan. Glancing head kick, Gurule felt that one. Hasan fires off another crowd-pleasing back kick to the body. Gurule strictly on defense through the first couple of minutes, Hasan’s strikes are coming out fast. Gurule closes the distance and lands a good left hand.

Hasan with more flashy stuff, mixing in his jab well. He lands a straight right. Gurule sneaks in a jab. Big overhand right by Gurule, that caught Hasan off-balance but should be a knockdown. Hasan recovers quickly, then clips Gurule with a head kick. Gurule throwing big punches, but Hasan with nice head movement to create whiffs. They’re exchanging kicks from distance.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Gurule.

Round 2

Inside low kick from Gurule scores. He drives in, but Hasan counters with a clinch and a few hard knees to the body. Gurule changes levels for a takedown attempt against the fence, great defense by Hasan and they’re back at range. Hasan with a good body kick. Gurule back to the inside leg kick. Hasan with a 360 roundhouse kick, mostly blocked, but that didn’t look fun to take. Gurule trying to time Hasan’s kicks. He catches one and pushes Hasan to the fence, followed by a couple of punches. Gurule scores a jab. Sweet spinning backfist by Hasan. Gurule deep on a takedown and he powers through to score it with 90 seconds left in the round. Hasan closes guard, just looking to neutralize any Gurule offense. Gurule maintaining control, but not doing any damage from top position. There’s a short elbow by Gurule, then another good punch. Gurule bullying Hasan as time ticks away. Close round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Gurule. Overall, 20-18 Gurule.

Round 3

Hasan with some urgency, right on the attack to open the final round. Gurule snatches a leg but Hasan with great balance to get out of there. However, Gurule right back in there and he catches Hasan with a right hand before scoring a takedown. Gurule taking his time, maintaining control, sneaking in strikes. Hasan doesn’t have a lot of answers right now. Time is ticking away with Gurule in top control and if Hasan didn’t bank the first two rounds, he’s in trouble. An entire round of top control for Gurule. I don’t expect the judges to have my card, but Gurule might have this.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Gurule. Overall, 30-27 Gurule.

Official result: Luis Gurule def. Bilal Hasan via split decision (28-29, 29-28 x2)

Post-fight

Gurule makes a joke about Hasan using ChatGPT to predict he would win.

“ChatGPT don’t know shit. F*ck the odds. F*ck the haters. We’re the 0.4, we’re the 0.4 in here, New York!”

“Look there’s only 10 people in here that f*cking believed in me, maybe the handful of people that I trained with, and it feels f*cking good. I dragged him into deep waters, I knew he couldn’t take it. I knew he couldn’t swim. … You’re only as good as your enemies, you’re only as good as your opponents, I want to say thank you to ‘The Indoninja.’”

Sergei Bilostenniy upset Vadim Nemkov to become the PFL heavyweight champion Saturday, beating the Fedor Emelianenko protege in the main event of the PFL Dubai card on Nov. 14.

Nemkov was quick to go for the takedown after a missed head kick early in the opening round, wasting no time before reaching full mount and going for the armbar, but Bilostenniy escaped and returned to his feet. Round two started strong for both Nemkov and Bilostenniy on the feet, with Bilostenniy finding more success in the stand-up while Nemkov shot for takedowns but failed to secure them over five minutes.

Bilostenniy easily stuffed a takedown attempt from Nemkov in round three, forcing the champion to stand with him. Neither fighter did much from that point on, apart from a head kick attempt for Nemkov that was blocked by Bilostenniy, while the challenger was the one to connect harder strikes. Bilostenniy continued to punish Nemkov on the feet in the fourth stanza, having to worry less about takedowns attempt from the champion.

The final round started and Nemkov, although leading when it comes to most strikes landed on official records, was behind in the scorecards with Bilostenniy scoring with most damaging strikes. Nemkov stayed on the outside, working with his jabs, and couldn’t secure a takedown. Both heavyweights were hesitant to go for it in the final minutes before time ran out.

In the end, judges declared Sergei Bilostenniy the new heavyweight champion via unanimous decision.

Patrick Habirora’s rise continues

Welterweight phenom Patrick Habirora continued his rise in the co-main event with a nasty finish of Omar El Dafrawy. The Belgium star came out strong and had to put his takedown defense to work early against El Dafrawy, but the guillotine choke proved to be the best counter to the takedowns when he put El Dafrawy out cold with a choke before the first round was over.

resultReports._summaryText:

Arman Tsarukyan needed less than one period to dispatch Neiman Gracie in the RAF Abu Dhabi co-main event.

While not surprising, Tsarukyan showed off his skills once again while taking on a much bigger opponent with Gracie struggling to keep any kind of momentum in the match.

A takedown from Tsarukyan and several turns just allowed him to accumulate points and get to 10-0 for the tech fall victory. Afterwards, Tsarukyan doubled down on his callout to potentially face Olympic champion Jordan Burroughs in the future.

“Nobody cares if he’s big or not,” Tsarukyan said about Gracie. “I always do my job. Size don’t matter, especially in wrestling. If I gave one point to him, I couldn’t look at [my coaches]. If [Jordan Burroughs] beats Zaurbek Sidakov, I’ll wrestle him.”

Tsarukyan started with a pushout before a snap takedown and he immediately started with his gut wrench turns to go up 7-0 in a hurry. A leg lace from Tsarukyan added another two points as his domination continued.

Up 9-0, Tsarukyan got another stepout for the final point to get the tech fall victory in the first period.

Tsarukyan remains one of the most active wrestlers on the entire RAF roster and it appears he’s going to keep it that way until he’s finally granted his UFC title shot, which might come in 2027.

This is the live blog for Khamzat Chimaev vs. Chris Weidman, the light heavyweight crossover championship main event for Saturday’s RAF Abu Dhabi match card at Etihad Arena. Weidman steps in on short notice for the injured Colby Covington.

Chimaev still gets to compete for a title despite Covington’s withdrawal as the promotion created a new crossover weight class championship. Chimaev is undefeated in his RAF run, including pinfall wins against Dillon Danis and Tyron Woodley, along with a tech fall victory against fellow former UFC champ Robbie Lawler this past month at RAF 14. “Borz” is staying busy as he awaits his next UFC opportunity after dropping the middleweight title to Sean Strickland in May at UFC 328.

Weidman makes his second RAF appearance. In his promotional debut, the former UFC middleweight champ dropped a super close match by points to Colby Covington at RAF 9 in May.

Check out the Khamzat Chimaev vs. Chris Weidman live blog below.

Round 1

Chris Weidman makes it to the mat first, and the lights go out! Here comes Khamzat Chimaev. “Borz” gives Weidman a hug when he hits the mat, and Weidman looks ready to go.

They lock up and it’s even early. Weidman faints to get Chimaev to bite, and Chimaev gets a quick escape point. They lock back up and it’s a battle for position. The whistle blows and they separate. Back at it they go and Chimaev skirts out of the way of Weidman and gets the back for two points. Referee stands it back up and the collar tie from Chimaev has been an effective weapon thus far, Chimaev gets two more points to go up 5-0.

Final 10 seconds and Weidman will be the first to make it to Round 2 against Chimaev.

Round 2

Weidman tries to get a takedown, but Chimaev reverses and gets a throw. As of now, Chimaev got four points, but it’s under review. After review, Chimaev got the escape point as well, and it’s 10-0. That’s a wrap! Chimaev wins and captures the light heavyweight crossover title.

Official Result: Khamzat Chimaev def. Chris Weidman via Tech Fall (10-0) – Round 2

Post-Match:

Chimaev is happy with the win. Chael Sonnen asks Chimaev who and what he wants next and he says he’ll wrestle or fight anybody.

That’s a wrap on RAF Abu Dhabi. Next event at the end of the month in Chicago.

resultReports._summaryText:

Tsarukyan, the current RAF middleweight crossover champion, competes in a non-title match just a few weeks removed from his tech fall championship win over Dillon Danis at RAF 14 in […]

This is the live blog for Arman Tsarukyan vs. Neiman Gracie, the catchweight co-main event for Saturday’s RAF Abu Dhabi wrestling event at Etihad Arena.

Tsarukyan, the current RAF middleweight crossover champion, competes in a non-title match just a few weeks removed from his tech fall championship win over Dillon Danis at RAF 14 in Las Vegas. “Batman” is 8-1 in the promotion, including tech fall wins over Tony Ferguson, Urijah Faber, and Lance Palmer. Tsarukyan is the top contender for the UFC lightweight title following his Knockout of the Year contending finish of Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331 in September.

Gracie, a longtime Bellator competitor and past title challenger, makes his sophomore appearance for Real American Freestyle. The jiu-jitsu ace dropped a decision in his promotional debut to Shara Magomedov at RAF Moscow in September.

Check out the Arman Tsarukyan vs. Neiman Gracie RAF Abu Dhabi live blog below.

Round 1

Neiman Gracie heads to the mat first, and here comes Arman Tsarukyan — who is a gigantic favorite to a custom Batman entrance video.

They lock up and Tsarukyan gets a quick point with a shove over the line. Collar tie on both ends, and Tsarukyan gets a front face lock, but Gracie is able to separate. Tsarukyan uses Gracie’s force against him to get two points, then rolls him over once. Twice now to go up 7-0. A third roll makes it 9-0.

Tsarukyan is a point away from victory. Gracie able to avoid things for a bit, but Tsarukyan forces him out of the circle to get the easy victory.

Official Result: Arman Tsarukyan def. Neiman Gracie via Tech Fall (10-0) Round 1, 1:56

Post-Match:

Tsarukyan speaks to Chael Sonnen and says despite Gracie being the bigger man, it “doesn’t matter.” Tsarukyan shouts out RAF for being a great promotion to compete for. “Batman” is looking for his belt and gets it. Tsarukyan then lays out what it will take for him to wrestle Jordan Borroughs, and if Borroughs wins his next match, he’ll wrestle him. If not, RAF should “fire” Borroughs.

resultReports._summaryText:
It’s been quite a week for Saba Lazashvili. Prior to Wednesday, he was an unknown Georgian wrestler and teammate to Merab Dvalishvili but after backing up the former UFC bantamweight champion when they were attacked by Usman Nurmagomegdov and members of his squad, the 21-year-old has suddenly become a household name. It’s been quite a week for Saba Lazashvili.

Prior to Wednesday, he was an unknown Georgian wrestler and teammate to Merab Dvalishvili but after backing up the former UFC bantamweight champion when they were attacked by Usman Nurmagomegdov and members of his squad, the 21-year-old has suddenly become a household name.

On Saturday, Lazashvili not only competed at RAF Abu Dhabi on short notice but he pulled off an upset win over former WEC champion Urijah Faber.

Down early in the match, Lazashvili stormed back in the third period after securing a takedown and then turning Faber several times to rack up a lot of points. In the end, Lazshvili went up 12-7 and Faber just couldn’t mount enough offense to prevent the loss.

“I want to say thank you to everybody coming here and supporting,” Lazashvili said after his win.”I’m really grateful for everything. [Merab] said I will be champion of the UFC in the future! I’ll wrestle everybody here.”

It was an ultra impressive showing, especially considering that Lazashvili wasn’t even supposed to compete when he arrived in Abu Dhabi but him taking out members of Nurmagomedov’s team during that brawl suddenly made him incredibly popular.

Now, he’s a winner in RAF, and it’s hard to believe this is the last major opportunity that Lazashvili receives in the aftermath of that brawl.

Terrance McKinney is lucky to still be fighting at UFC 334.

Saturday’s event is headlined by a pair of title fights featuring Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit, and Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes, but McKinney caused a stir at Friday’s official weigh-ins for the wrong reasons. The all-action lightweight registered at 160.2 pounds on the scale, more than four pounds over the limit for his preliminary bout with Jim Miller (155.6).

Fortunately for McKinney, Miller has agreed to proceed with the bout at a catchweight with McKinney forfeiting 30 percent of his purse.

McKinney was quick to release a statement to social media apologizing to Miller and declaring that he will soon move up to the 170-pound division. See McKinney’s comments and watch his weigh-in below.

“I want to apologize to everyone and UFC for missing weight,” McKinney wrote. “I’ve never missed weight in my life and I’m sorry, but ship has sailed for 155. It’s official, my last bout at lightweight. I’m trusting in God will make sure I’m ready for whatever comes at welterweight.”

“I want to thank Jim Miller personally for still taking the fight. He’s a real gangster and also want to apologize to him for failing to make. Jim f*cking Miller GOATed, appreciate you for letting dream still be a reality fighting at MSG.”

One other preliminary fighter, Juan Diaz, also missed weight, coming in 0.4 pounds over the 135-pound limit (including one-pound allowance for a non-title fight). His bout with Alatengheili proceeds as a catchweight with Diaz forfeiting 20 percent of his purse as penalty.

Gane and Hokit both took their time arriving at Friday’s weigh-ins, but had no issues making weight for the heavyweight title main event, coming in well under the 265-pounds limit with Gane at 242.6 and Hokit at 231.4.

The first two fighters to weigh in were Harrison and Nunes, who both hit championship weight at 135 pounds on the dot. Harrison defends her bantamweight championship for the first time, while Nunes, a former two-division champion, competes in her first bout since announcing a retirement in June 2023.

resultReports.title: ONE Fight Night 49 MMA And Submission Grappling Results: Lee, Czaban, Hugo, And Israilov Shine In Bangkok
resultReports._summaryText:
These four stars catapulted themselves closer to ONE World Title gold on Friday, November 6.

ONE Fight Night 49: Gabriel vs. Magomedov went down live in U.S. primetime from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday, November 6, and the card’s MMA and submission grappling action kept the energy high from beginning to end.

A heavyweight grappling trilogy between a pair of World Champions was settled in a flash, ending a rivalry nearly a decade in the making.

Plus, two undefeated debutants squared off in a grinding bantamweight clash with a perfect record on the line, while an unbeaten rising star went the distance in a tightly contested atomweight chess match. Finally, a strawweight clash that opened with a grappling scare ended in a choke and could lead to a World Title opportunity.

Here’s what happened in the MMA and submission grappling matches at ONE Fight Night 49.

Lee Sinks In Rear-Naked Choke To Submit Lalthazuala

“The Flash” Lee Seung Cheol may have just earned a crack at the ONE Strawweight MMA World Title. The South Korean handed Nazareth “The Northstar” Lalthazuala his first career loss, as he submitted the Indian phenom via rear-naked choke in the second round of a match that was filled with plot twists.

Most of the opening frame was spent on the canvas, with Lalthazuala hunting for submissions and even getting close to securing a choke. The Indian MMA star looked like he’d be gliding toward an easy win. But Lee weathered the storm, and he returned more determined in the second stanza.

The 27-year-old South Korean had his opponent trapped against the ropes and rained down ground-and-pound. Lalthazuala threw up-kicks until he could create enough space to stand, but the two soon went back to the mat and battled for position. Lee won that battle, as he took the back of the 25-year-old and sunk in the choke for the tap at the 3:04 mark of round two.

That submission win moved Lee’s record to 14-1, put him on a 14-bout winning streak, and inched him closer to a shot at ONE Strawweight MMA World Champion Joshua Pacio, who will defend his belt at ONE SAMURAI 5 on November 18.

Czaban Edges Souza In Close Battle, Remains Undefeated

Polish star Magdalena “The Powerpuff Girl” Czaban outpointed Brazilian rival Vick Souza over three tightly contested rounds to take a unanimous decision victory in their atomweight MMA clash and keep her unblemished professional record intact.

Once the opening bell sounded, Souza hunted her opponent’s legs with low kicks. However, the 27-year-old Polish fighter responded with a variety of punches and kicks. Soon, the 29-year-old Brazilian hit a takedown, pinned “The Powerpuff Girl” to the canvas, and searched for the finish.

Czaban stayed on the outside in round two, pelting the Brazilian with combinations. Souza fired back with counters, and the two battled neck and neck. The third and final frame was another back-and-forth affair, as “The Powerpuff Girl” stung her foe with jabs and the Brazilian continued to throw inside low kicks.

In the end, all three judges gave the nod to Czaban, who registered her second straight win in ONE Championship, moved her record to 6-0, and took another step forward on the path toward becoming Poland’s first ONE World Champion.

Hugo Submits Johnson In Trilogy

Seven-time BJJ World Champion Victor Hugo waited nearly a decade to face American rival, former IBJJF No-Gi World Champion Devhonte Johnson, in a trilogy match and settle their unfinished business. At ONE Fight Night 49, the Brazilian finally got his wish and made the most of the opportunity.

A foot sweep set up the finish, as Hugo submitted his longtime adversary via rear-naked choke at the 1:35 mark of their openweight submission grappling contest.

Hugo – the reigning ADCC World Champion – used the sweep to put Johnson on the canvas and quickly took his back. The two promotional newcomers then waged a hand-fighting battle for control, until the 29-year-old Brazilian locked in the choke and cranked down on the jaw of the 32-year-old American, who was forced to tap.

The victory broke a 1-1 tie in a rivalry that began in their purple belt days, when Hugo took the first meeting at the 2016 IBJJF Worlds and Johnson won the rematch at the 2017 Europeans. The Brazilian waited nine years for a third encounter, and he won so emphatically in a bout that could help usher in ONE Championship’s heavyweight submission grappling division. It also moved his record to 101-23.

Israilov Stays Perfect With Hard-Fought Win Over Tabarov

French rising star Ilmadi Israilov kept his spotless record alive in the opening bout of the night, as he claimed a unanimous decision victory over Tajik sensation Kalandar Tabarov in a bantamweight MMA clash between two more undefeated promotional newcomers.

Israilov spent the better part of the battle hunting for the single-leg takedown, while his 27-year-old foe stuffed shots and fought out of scrambles. The 23-year-old Frenchman landed the takedown on several occasions and tried to pummel his opponent with ground-and-pound, but Tabarov defended the attacks well.

An accidental kick to the face of the grounded Tajik cost Israilov a yellow card, though it did little to slow him down. By the final bell, he was right back on the offensive, pinning his opponent to the canvas and searching for a finish with ground-and-pound.

The judges were unanimous in their scoring, and the victory moved Israilov’s career record to 10-0 in his ONE Championship debut.

We’re back in U.S. primetime! Follow along for breaking news and updates!

After kicking off the month with two explosive shows and a heart-racing MMA World Title bout, ONE Championship closes out its triple-header weekend with ONE Fight Night 49: Gabriel vs. Magomedov.

The world’s largest martial arts organization will broadcast ONE Fight Night 49: Gabriel vs. Magomedov live in U.S. primetime from Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, November 6.

In the main event, Brazilian contender Lucas Gabriel will face undefeated star Magomed Magomedov, and the winner could get the next ONE Lightweight MMA World Championship opportunity.

Before that, in the co-main event, Taiki “Silent Sniper” Naito will go head-to-head with Kongthoranee Sor Sommai in a flyweight kickboxing rematch. This serves as the sequel to their 2023 Muay Thai clash, which the Thai veteran won.

Plus, unbeaten warriors Magdalena Czaban, Kalandar Tabarov, Ilmadi Israilov, and Nazareth Lalthazuala will look to maintain their spotless records. And seven-time BJJ World Champion Victor Hugo will make his ONE Championship debut.
